summary.title: Cache-aware Roofline model: Upgrading the loft
summary.one_liner: The paper extends the Roofline performance model with a separate roof for each cache level, so kernels that hit in cache are not plotted as DRAM bound.
takeaways: Classic Roofline plots against DRAM traffic only, which can misclassify kernels whose working set fits in cache.
The cache-aware variant adds a bandwidth roof per cache level, measured against traffic at the core.
The model is meant to give insight into system performance capabilities to guide application and architecture optimization.
summary.summary: The page is the IEEE Xplore entry for a paper titled "Cache-aware Roofline model: Upgrading the loft". The text visible here is only the introduction, which motivates performance models as tools for understanding how applications use diverse microprocessor capabilities. The listing notes that the paper adds a roof per cache level against core-side traffic, so cache-resident kernels are not plotted as DRAM bound. The visible text does not include the model's equations, experiments, or results.
